correctness.rationale: Legendre kernel integration telescopes exactly to (P_n+P_{n+1})/2; Chebyshev endpoint evaluation reduces to the integrated Dirichlet kernel. On a Lipschitz unit ball, choosing the sign of each integrated kernel as the derivative achieves the L1 integral. Jacobi Darboux asymptotics plus endpoint domination give sqrt(2/pi), while Abel summation with a small-angle split gives 8/pi². Direct finite quadrature verified degrees 0,1,2,5,10,20,50,100 and the exact n=2 Legendre radical, but the analytic steps prove the general claims. No all-position uniform bound is asserted.

value.rationale: The natural worst-case endpoint recovery problem over all unit-Lipschitz inputs admits attaining extremizers and exact constants for every polynomial degree. The calculated sharp rates distinguish two conventional spectral projections acting on exactly the same inputs: Legendre loses a square-root power relative to Chebyshev, with both leading constants evaluated. This is a substantive operator-stability distinction and provides optimal quantitative guidance rather than an isolated low-degree table entry.
